task: DAEO-uzme (W2-70) round 2: revise W1-01's merge rule (`merge_offences`) so a merge passes when its acceptance files equal git's own merge of its parents (DEC-912 item 1), with the KPI line's four fixture cases.

(b) `git hash-object -w --stdin` worked (blob `1ae28402a109`, exit 0) and `git update-index --refresh` exited 0. `GOV_ROLE=independent-test-designer`, `GOV_TICKET=DAEO-uzme`; the toplevel is `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-70` on `w2/W2-70`; HEAD was `11800d25`. `gov.__file__` = `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-70/src/gov/__init__.py`. I added the fixture cases first and ran them on the unchanged rule; case 1 was red (see evidence). Then I revised `merge_offences`. A new helper, `_git_merge_under`, runs `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only -z --no-messages <first> <other>` and is called only when a file fails today's parent check and the merge has exactly two parents. A failing file passes if it is not in git's conflicted list and its mode and blob (or absence) equal git's tree. No allowance is given for an octopus merge, a git error, no merge base, or a git without `--write-tree`; the file is then judged as today. The brought-commit half, the offence line format, `acceptance_exemptions`, `acceptance_test_offenders` and the path map are unchanged. The docstring states the rule and cites DEC-912 item 1 with DEC-750 and DEC-754.

Red before the change: `test_a_clean_merge_of_two_designers_edits_of_one_file_passes[clean]` and `[conflict-outside-the-folder]` both failed with `['the merge commit itself changes tests/acceptance/W1-94/test_shared.py']`. The merged file is git's clean merge of the two designers' edits, so it equals neither parent's copy, which is all today's rule accepts. Case 4 was also red then, with two offences (that "itself changes" line plus the commit) where one is expected; cases 2 and 3 passed (still refused) before and after.
tests: Before the change, the new cases alone: 3 failed, 3 passed. After the change, `tests/acceptance/W1-01` run whole: 66 passed, 28 skipped, 0 failed, in 20.5 s. Every skip is the folder's existing "W1-05 is closed: the interim guardrail is retired (DEC-084)" skip; none is a new case.
discoveries: `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only -z --no-messages` on git 2.43 prints the tree id then each conflicted path, each ending in NUL. It exits 1 on a conflict and 128 for unrelated histories. Conflict markers carry the labels of the arguments given, so a check that compares blobs depends on calling merge-tree with full commit ids; the rule and the tests both do. `gov retrieve` (asked "W1-01 merge rule merge_offences git merge-tree DEC-912") returned no evidence because its lexical and semantic facets are stale, so I read the named files directly.
risks: merge-tree writes tree and blob objects into the repository's object store when the history case meets a merge that fails today's check; they are unreferenced and git's gc removes them. Git's merge follows the repository's merge config (renames, conflict style), so a config change between the merge and the check could change git's tree. Neither real merge was in this branch's history, so I have not confirmed by run that `03f470a5` and `4ef3293a` turn green; the src-conflict fixture models the first of them.
lessons: No earlier test was rewritten; every change is an addition. Beyond the KPI line's four cases I added two variants, each a parameter of an existing case. Case 1 has a second form with a content conflict in `src/` resolved by hand, the shape of one of the real merges; it shows a conflict outside the folder does not take the allowance away. Case 3 has a second form whose resolution is git's own conflict-marker text for the file, to pin that a file git reports as conflicted gets no allowance even when it equals git's tree byte for byte. I made no edits to `test_w1_01_history.py`, `README.md`, any other folder or the path map.
